message.content:
The signal can be written as

\[
x(t)=\left(\frac{\sin(50\pi t)}{\pi t}\right)^2
\]

We know

\[
\frac{\sin(50\pi t)}{\pi t} \longleftrightarrow \text{rectangular spectrum of bandwidth } 50\pi
\]

Squaring in time corresponds to convolution in frequency, so the bandwidth doubles:

\[
X(j\omega)=0 \quad \text{for } |\omega|>100\pi
\]

Thus \(x(t)\) is bandlimited to

\[
\omega_m = 100\pi
\]

The sampling frequency is

\[
\omega_s = 150\pi
\]

For impulse sampling,

\[
G(j\omega)=\frac{1}{T_s}\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}X(j(\omega-k\omega_s))
\]

Since

\[
T_s=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_s}=\frac{2\pi}{150\pi}=\frac{1}{75}
\]

we have

\[
G(j\omega)=75\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}X(j(\omega-k\omega_s))
\]

For \(G(j\omega)=75X(j\omega)\), there must be no aliasing contribution from shifted copies. The first shifted copy begins at

\[
\omega_s-\omega_m = 150\pi-100\pi=50\pi
\]

Therefore, the spectrum is undistorted only for

\[
|\omega|\le 50\pi
\]

So the maximum value of \(\omega_0\) is

\[
\omega_0=50\pi
\]

Answer: A
